subject: Shanghai Moon Extended Hours Special Permit
overview: The Council approved a special permit for extended hours at Shanghai Moon following a mediated compromise between the owners and neighbors. The body also authorized the 2015 city election call and initiated studies on business tax abatements and solar energy feasibility.

items.title: Brooks Estate residency settlement
items.summary: Tabled a $24,000 settlement regarding residency at the Brooks Estate to allow the Solicitor to provide the Council with an updated agreement.

items.title: Spring Street Super-Red Keno license
items.summary: Approved a Keno monitor license for 88 Spring Street following the acquisition of necessary zoning variances.

items.title: Shanghai Moon extended hours permit
items.summary: Approved a special permit for extended hours at 442 Salem Street with conditions including a 90-day probationary midnight closing and an 11:00 PM cutoff for karaoke.

items.title: Business tax abatement study
items.summary: Approved a resolution to study the feasibility of tax abatements as a tool to attract businesses to vacant storefronts.

items.title: Medford High School solar energy
items.summary: Approved a feasibility study for installing solar panels on the roof of Medford High School and exploring hydropower options.

items.title: Tedeschi Food Shop license
items.summary: Approved a 24-hour common victualler license for the Tedeschi Food Shop at 213 Main Street.

items.title: Robert Emmett Skerry and Tony Bova honors
items.summary: Congratulated Robert Emmett Skerry on his retirement and requested the mayor name the circle at LaConte Rink in honor of youth hockey volunteer Tony Bova.

items.title: 2015 City Election call
items.summary: Authorized the official call for the November 3 municipal election, including the Community Preservation Act ballot question.

items.title: Haines Square improvements and safety
items.summary: Referred requests for improved parking lot lighting, sidewalk repairs, and a police update on neighborhood crime to the administration and subcommittees.

items.title: Public safety building needs
items.summary: Heard a presentation regarding the necessity of a new 911 center and police/fire station facility to address public safety morale and infrastructure needs.

items.title: Condolences and minutes
items.summary: Issued condolences to the families of Catherine Scaramuzzo and Carmella Milly Natarelli and approved meeting minutes from July and September meetings.

items.title: Pedestrian safety and traffic monitoring
items.summary: Requested updates on pedestrian signaling at Forest Street and directed police to monitor speeding and potential drag racing on Washington Street.

items.title: Vacant commercial building update
items.summary: Requested a status update from the Building Commissioner regarding the vacant storefront located near Main Street and Tedeschi's.
